findings.claim: DUP=D1 treats the three queued D1 files as separate planning attempts and gives them new identities TASK-0089…0091 with status `queued`. The sources this proposal already cites show they are the same TASK identity. `R-0007/plan.md:1039-1041`: 'TASK-0002-D1 = TASK-0020; TASK-0003-D1 = TASK-0021; TASK-0004-D1 = TASK-0022. Filenames pedidos permanecem; id/upstream_task_id e compositions usam IDs numéricos'. `plan.md:1324-1325`: 'TASK-0019, PREP-CTG1-D1 e TASK-0020 concluídos'. The R-0007 budget.json ledger records the D1 executions under those same ids: idx 37 TASK-0019, 39 TASK-0020 completed, 40 PREP-CTG1-D1, 41 TASK-0021 completed_iteration_1, 42 TASK-0022 completed-fail. After that come TASK-0020-ITERATION-2…13, a single lineage. `plan.md:378` says the TASK-0020/21/22 JSONs were materialized 'preservando 3/4, 3/4 e 1/4'. Those are exactly the iteration_count/max_iterations of the three D1 stubs (3/4, 3/4, 1/4); the stubs also carry `alias-TASK-000n-D1` and `c4-od-v3` tags and point to the prompts `TASK-002n-V3.md`. So the stubs are superseded snapshots of TASKs that did run and were later rematerialized, not distinct unexecuted TASKs. The proposal's reading ('não prova que os D1 queued foram executados… tentativas de planejamento distintas') leaves out this evidence. Creating 0089…0091 as `queued` invents three unexecuted historical TASKs. Remapping the upstreams TASK-0020→0089 and TASK-0021→0090 invents edges that plan §1040 says point to the numeric identity. The 29/92 cycle counts, the example 0090↔0091, and 'zero ciclos upstream com 91 IDs únicos' all rest on these invented nodes. It also enlarges the dispatch surface: `materializeRoundQueueTask` (release-host.js ~188268) accepts only valid `queued` TASKs in an active round, so under G0 these three would be the only materializable R-0007 TASKs until the seal.
findings.fix: Reformulate DUP. The primary option should treat the three D1 files as superseded snapshots of the canonical identities TASK-0020/0021/0022. Preserve them byte-for-byte in the A3 sidecar with an index that cites plan §§378, 1039-1041 and 1324-1325 and ledger idx 37-42 (hash each). Retire the direct paths and do not project any new canonical TASK, alias ID or remapped upstream. Also state that the stubs' `queued` status is a literal from a superseded snapshot. Recompute the cycle counts and the upstream DAG over 88 unique IDs (28/91 as measured in cycle 1). If the Owner does not accept 'superseded snapshot', keep D2 source_pending. Do not offer distinct queued aliases unless a new source shows the D1 files are separate work.

findings.claim: G0 checks for non-materialization only in `.devai/state/tasks`. But `materializeRoundQueueTask` (~188268-188300) also writes `.devai/state/backlog.jsonl` (`appendBacklog`, BACKLOG_PATH_REL ~176475) and checks conflicts against it. A materialization attempt that created a backlog entry, or one reverted from the tasks store only, would escape the guard as written. `.devai/state` is versioned (tracked files under `audit-observations/`), so the check is verifiable, but only if it covers every state path the verbs write to.
findings.fix: Extend the G0 static guard to every `.devai/state` path the materialize/start/run verbs write (at minimum `tasks/` and `backlog.jsonl`). The Inspector should derive the list from the pinned runtime, and the guard must fail on any R-0007 entry.
